# Mastalgia

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Obstetrics/gynecology > Breast disorders > Mastalgia*

[Original Article Link](/library/qG0CZ3)

---

## Summary

Mastalgia is defined as <u>breast</u> <u>pain</u> or discomfort. It is often caused by physiological changes (e.g., hormonal effects, lactation), but can also result from underlying disease (e.g., benign inflammatory <u>breast</u> conditions). Mastalgia is classified as cyclical (associated with <u>menstrual cycles</u>), noncyclical (not associated with <u>menstrual cycles</u>), or extramammary (originating outside of the <u>breast</u>, such as the <u>chest wall</u>). Imaging is required for all patients with an associated <u>palpable breast mass</u>. In patients without a palpable mass, <u>cyclical mastalgia</u> typically requires no further evaluation while <u>breast</u> imaging may be indicated in women with <u>noncyclical mastalgia</u>. Evaluation of extramammary <u>pain</u> depends on the suspected source of <u>pain</u> (e.g., musculoskeletal, pulmonary). Treatment commonly involves reassurance, <u>analgesics</u>, and management of the underlying etiology. In patients with severe or persistent <u>pain</u>, hormonal therapy (e.g., <u>danazol</u>, <u>tamoxifen</u>) may be considered under specialist guidance.

---

## Etiology

* Cyclical mastalgia: primary <u>breast</u> <u>pain</u> associated with <u>the menstrual cycle</u>

* Hormonal fluctuations of <u>the menstrual cycle</u>

* <u>Postmenopausal</u> <u>hormone</u> therapy

* <u>Oral contraceptive</u> use

* Noncyclical mastalgia: primary <u>breast</u> <u>pain</u> not associated with <u>the menstrual cycle</u>

* Inflammatory <u>breast</u> conditions

* <u>Mastitis</u>

* <u>Breast abscess</u>

* <u>Mammary duct ectasia</u>

* <u>Superficial thrombophlebitis</u> (<u>Mondor disease of the breast</u>)

* <u>Breast</u> lumps or cysts

* Pendulous <u>breasts</u>

* Medications (e.g., <u>hormone replacement therapy</u>, <u>oral contraceptives</u>)

* Previous <u>breast</u> <u>surgery</u>

* <u>Breast cancer</u> (uncommon)

* Extramammary <u>pain</u>: secondary <u>breast</u> <u>pain</u> referred from extramammary locations

* <u>Costochondritis</u>

* <u>Chest wall</u> trauma

* <u>Shingles</u>

* Cardiac, esophageal, or pulmonary causes

---

## Clinical features

* <u>Cyclical mastalgia</u> [[4]](/library/x21EPT0)

* Often bilateral, diffuse <u>breast</u> <u>pain</u>

* Typically most severe in the upper outer quadrant of <u>the breasts</u>

* May radiate to the <u>medial</u> aspect of the upper arm

* Usually worsens the week prior to the onset of <u>menstruation</u>

* <u>Noncyclical mastalgia</u> [[4]](/library/x21EPT0)

* Unilateral or bilateral <u>breast</u> <u>pain</u>, usually located over the costal <u>cartilage</u>

* Sharp or burning <u>pain</u> and/or soreness

* Extramammary <u>pain</u>: depends on the underlying condition

---

## Diagnosis

### Clinical assessment [[3]](/library/Qe1uAf0)[[4]](/library/x21EPT0)




* <u>Patient history</u>

* Nature of <u>pain</u>

* Recent musculoskeletal injury or trauma; see also “<u>Fat necrosis of the breast</u>”

* Association with <u>menstruation</u>

* <u>Family history</u> of <u>breast cancer</u>

* <u>Medication review</u>

* Focused <u>physical examination</u>

* <u>Clinical breast examination</u> (see also “<u>Breast cysts</u>” and “<u>Mastitis</u>”)

* <u>Musculoskeletal examination</u> of the <u>chest wall</u>





> [!TIP]
> Examine the <u>chest wall</u> in all patients with mastalgia to evaluate for extramammary sources of <u>pain</u>. [[3]](/library/Qe1uAf0)




### Imaging [[4]](/library/x21EPT0)[[5]](/library/Ut1b1i0)[[6]](/library/hM1coh0)




#### <u>Palpable breast mass</u>




* Imaging is indicated for all patients.

* See “<u>Palpable breast mass</u>” for details.





#### No <u>palpable breast mass</u>




* <u>Cyclical mastalgia</u>: no imaging necessary (regardless of age)

* Focal <u>noncyclical mastalgia</u>

* Age < 30 years: <u>breast ultrasound</u>

* Age ≥ 30 years: <u>breast ultrasound</u>, <u>diagnostic mammography</u>, or <u>digital breast tomosynthesis</u>  [[6]](/library/hM1coh0)

* Nonfocal  or diffuse <u>noncyclical mastalgia</u>

* Age ≥ 40 years or <u>risk factors for breast cancer</u>: <u>diagnostic mammography</u>

* Age < 40 years: no imaging necessary





> [!TIP]
> Imaging is indicated for all patients with mastalgia and a <u>palpable breast mass</u>. [[3]](/library/Qe1uAf0)

---

## Treatment

### Initial management [[3]](/library/Qe1uAf0)[[4]](/library/x21EPT0)




* Identify and treat the underlying etiology.

* Nonpharmacological measures 

* Reassurance  [[3]](/library/Qe1uAf0)[[4]](/library/x21EPT0)[[7]](/library/rk1f6S0)

* Use of a supportive, well-fitting bra

* Adjust causative medications, if feasible.  [[3]](/library/Qe1uAf0)

* <u>Analgesics</u>

* First-line : topical <u>NSAIDs</u>  [[4]](/library/x21EPT0)

* Alternatives: oral <u>NSAIDs</u> or <u>acetaminophen</u> [[3]](/library/Qe1uAf0)

* See “<u>Pain management</u>” for details and dosages.





### Management of moderate, severe, or refractory symptoms



* Consider gynecology referral for hormonal treatment (e.g., <u>tamoxifen</u>, <u>danazol</u>, or <u>goserelin</u>).  [[3]](/library/Qe1uAf0)[[4]](/library/x21EPT0)
